newsitem.title: FINLAND: PONSSE SAYS SEES 1997 PROFITS UP ON '96.
newsitem.headline: PONSSE SAYS SEES 1997 PROFITS UP ON '96.

text.p: Finnish forest harvester maker Ponsse Oy said on Tuesday it expected its full-year 1997 earnings to improve on 1996 and net sales to exceed 400 million markka.

"Because of the record orderbook, new products and succesful export efforts, net sales are expected to grow to over 400 million markka and the earnings to improve on the previous year," Ponsse said in a statement with its January-April results.

Ponsse said it expected the slump in the pulp and paper industry to continue far into the year, but demand for sawn goods and vaneer were likely to remain at their current, high level at least until late autumn.

"Timber cuttings in our main markets will probably remain stable, at least at the 1996 level. Demand for forest harvesting machines is likewise expected to remain strong throughout the year," it said.
Ponsse reported January-April profits before extraordinary items and tax down to 12.1 million markka from 16.6 million in the year-ago period.
Ponsee's 1996 profit before extraordinary items was 36.8 million markka and net sales were 372.5 million markka.
